issue.title: Break up the 497-module src/sase import cycle
issue.description: src/sase has a single import cycle spanning 497 modules, which the epic plan for sase-fp (Test suite Tier 1 -- two-speed verification with diff-scoped test selection) identified as the root cause of static import-graph-based test selection being unsound: any module inside the cycle transitively 'imports' every other module in the cycle, so a change anywhere in it selects far more tests than the change actually touches (or, if broken apart naively, could miss tests). Breaking the cycle into smaller, real dependency components would let static selection be both cheaper and more precise. Proposed by epic sase-fp's land phase (sase-fp.8.3); named directly in the epic plan plans:202608/test_suite_tier1.md.

evidence.note: Epic sase-g3 measured the cost of this import cycle directly, and it survives the epic's own mitigation. 'just selection-backtest' replays real commits and compares the diff-scoped selection against per-test coverage ground truth; with --include-descendant-baseline over the last 100 commits at 625b5cac40fb, closure-only recall is perfect on 29 of 31 usable commits but still blind-spots on two AFTER phase compensate's no-baseline-depth-boost (depth+1) is active: 9a366e0d6c5a 'fix(ace): resolve Artifacts project scope through project refs' at 57.1% recall (missed 9 of 21 ground-truth test files) and 840cdff10664 'fix(commit-finalizer): break async-wait deadlock in finalizer passes' at 85.7% (missed 1 of 7). Both fit the widely-executed-but-shallowly-imported shape this bead names as root cause. The sharpest case is src/sase/ace/tui/_app_layout.py, where 42 of 91 covering test files stay outside the depth-3 closure. Phase compensate measured and REJECTED the obvious workaround: directory-mirror expansion of tests/ace/tui/** is 831 files = 35.7% of the suite, above the 0.25 escalation ratio, so it degenerates into a full run. Depth is therefore exhausted as a lever short of breaking the cycle. Proposed by sase-g3.3/sase-g3.5, corroborated at land time by sase-g3.land.
